links.outcome: Accuracy and retained sample fraction when deferring high-uncertainty seizure predictions for clinical evaluation
links.effect: Selective classification raised accuracy from 91.7% (baseline) to 99.6% while retaining ~74% of samples, outperforming models optimized for calibration or uncertainty alone.
links.quote: The selective classification improved accuracy from 91.7% (baseline) to 99.6% while retaining ∼74% of samples, outperforming models optimized for either calibration or uncertainty alone.

unlisted_practices: Selecting Monte Carlo dropout rate via multi-objective optimization of Expected Calibration Error and entropy-based overlap area between correct and misclassified samples

screen.practice: uncertainty-based selective classification / referral for clinical review
screen.reason: The study develops and tests an uncertainty quantification and selective classification safeguard that flags low-confidence predictions to defer them for human clinical review, measuring its impact on model accuracy and coverage.
